survey: A green canvas camping armchair, shown three-quarter from the front-left and resting on a flat floor. Backrest: a canvas sleeve slid over two upright metal back posts, each with a grey end cap on top. Seat: a canvas sling stretched between the side rails. The front corners show a tube end, which reads as a front crossbar hidden in the hem. Sides: each side has its own X-frame with a visible pivot bolt where the tubes cross (left pivot at mid-height, right pivot under the seat). On each side, the back post runs down past the seat and becomes the leg that reaches the front foot. The front tube curves up from the seat corner into the armrest support and runs down to the back foot. The two sides mirror each other. Armrests: padded green tops, joined at the back to the back posts and resting at the front on the curved front tubes. Feet: four grey rubber caps, all touching the floor, with shadows that match. Count: 2 back posts, 2 armrests, 2 X-frames, 4 feet. All are correct and nothing is extra. Every tube starts and ends at a joint, a pivot or a foot, and nothing floats or passes through anything else. The armrests are fixed to both posts, which would keep a side-X frame from folding. Like the three-button phone, that is an accepted simplification, because the chair stands, carries a sitter and reads as a folding camp chair.
